title: Enterprise dedicated intake playbook: SLA banding, GPU-fit scoring, and scaling policy proposals
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Objective: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for enterprise dedicated capacity requests. Scope focuses on non-bug feature requests for Reserved Pools: mapping customer requirements to SLA bands, reserved throughput sizing, GPU-family recommendations, and autoscaling policy templates. This doc will drive intake form updates, a scoring rubric, and a runbook for handoff to Capacity Concierge and Solutions Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake form template with required fields for SLA targets, traffic profile, and cost constraints
A scoring rubric that outputs a prioritized band (bronze/silver/gold) and recommended GPU family
Example sizing for three representative workloads (low-latency chat, high-throughput embedding, mixed bursty inference)
Clear autoscaling policy templates and burst-credit guidance for each band
Sign-off from Solutions Engineering and Capacity Operations on the proposed playbook
triage_rubric: Score components: business criticality (0-30), latency SLO strictness (0-25), predictable throughput (0-20), data isolation/regulatory (0-15), price sensitivity (0-10). Tally -> Band mapping: 0-40 = Bronze (best-effort, shared fallback), 41-70 = Silver (reserved pool with constrained burst), 71-100 = Gold (dedicated pool, SLA-backed), with explicit GPU-fit recommendation rules per band.
gpu_recommendations: Low-latency (<50ms p95), small context: prefer H100-80GB or A100-80GB depending on model; target single-GPU placement with KV-cache warming
High-throughput batching (embeddings, log processing): prefer multi-A100 or multi-H100 pools with optimized batching kernels
Cost-sensitive large context workloads: recommend quantized L4/NPU class models for inference (where model family supports) or scaled A10/NVIDIA L series
sizing_examples: Chat assistant (p95 latency 150ms, steady 50 req/s, spikes to 400 req/s): Silver band; reserve 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with burst credit configured for 8x short bursts; suggest prefix/KV cache and 4s pre-warm window
Embeddings pipeline (3500 vectors/s steady, large batch throughput required): Gold band; reserve 8x A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale min=6, max=12 and background batch worker pool
Regulated batch inference (nightly completes within 2 hours, high privacy): Bronze->Silver negotiation; recommend reserved 4x GPUs during window with ephemeral burst capacity for retries
scaling_policies: Autoscale-on-queue-depth: target concurrency thresholds per GPU family with cool-down of 60s; prefer vertical scaling (add GPUs) for Gold band
Burst credit model: maintain a burst bucket measured in GPU-seconds; Silver gets limited burst (3x baseline for 60s), Gold gets higher burst and pre-warm options

Fallback routing: when reserved pool saturated, route to compatible hosted model variants (lower-cost quantized) per customer policy; include sticky region fallback for data residency-sensitive customers
tradeoffs_and_risks: Over-committing GPUs increases cost; conservative sizing may cause customer-visible throttling—need clear SLA tradeoff disclosure
GPU family lock-in (e.g., H100-only) reduces scheduling flexibility during cloud constraints; include recommended fallbacks in contract
Autoscale oscillation risk if thresholds are mis-tuned; require monitoring + canary enablement for new customers
rollout_plan: Q1: Finalize intake form and rubric; pilot with two existing enterprise customers (one embeddings-heavy, one chat-heavy)
Q2: Integrate scoring into onboarding dashboard, add Capacity Concierge UI for manual overrides
Q3: Publish public-facing SLA bands and update contract templates; instrument cost/latency dashboards for post-onboarding monitoring
metrics: Onboarding time (lead -> pool provisioned) target: < 7 business days for Silver, < 3 business days for Gold
Post-onboarding SLO compliance rate: 99% monthly for Gold, 95% for Silver
Cost variance vs estimate: within +/-15% for 80% of onboardings after 30 days
